answer: A work-bond vault makes Sybil attacks expensive in an agent economy. Before an agent can accept paid tasks, it locks a bond in a shared vault; the bond is returned only after independent peers verify the completed work. A single operator spinning up a grove of fake identities must fund a separate bond for each one, and every failed or abandoned job slashes that bond. Honest agents build a lasting record in the vault and earn haven status: lower bonds and priority access to high-value work. Forging a hundred identities costs a hundred bonds, while a real agent pays once and keeps its standing.
